description.value: Remote campsite beside the Nahwitti River in northern Vancouver Island's old-growth backcountry, reached by rough logging roads with no confirmed services or drinking water.

address.value: Cape Scott Provincial Park, Mount Waddington, BC, Canada

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM record identifies this as a camp_site within Cape Scott Provincial Park, linking to the BC Parks Cape Scott page. The website confirms Cape Scott Park is an active wilderness park at the northwestern tip of Vancouver Island, but contains no content specific to the Nahwitti River Campsite sub-location — amenity details for this individual backcountry site cannot be confirmed from the available evidence. The park's wilderness/backcountry character (described explicitly on the site) means frontcountry amenities like showers, laundry, and device charging are very unlikely, but absence of evidence requires null rather than false.
concerns: The linked website covers all of Cape Scott Park and contains no content specific to Nahwitti River Campsite — no amenity, reservation, or access details can be confirmed for this individual site.

This appears to be a backcountry wilderness campsite accessible only by multi-day hiking trail, which significantly limits its utility for most touring cyclists and raises questions about directional access by bike.
No address or phone number in OSM record; the BC Parks general contact (1-800-689-9025, parkinfo@gov.bc.ca) is available from the website but is not campsite-specific.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: This is a legitimate backcountry campsite within an active provincial park and could serve adventurous cycle tourists, but the BC Parks website contains no content specific to the Nahwitti River Campsite sub-location, leaving all amenity fields unverifiable. A reviewer should confirm whether the site is realistically bikepacking-accessible and whether a dedicated campsite page exists.
enrichment_extras.notes: BC Parks general contact from website: phone 1-800-689-9025 (toll-free Canada/US), email parkinfo@gov.bc.ca. Nearest communities with accommodation are Port Hardy, Port McNeill, Holberg, and Port Alice per the Cape Scott Park page.
